title: Lantern-shaped 3d–4f high-nuclearity clusters with magnetocaloric effect

synthesis.procedure: Gd2O3, nickel acetate tetrahydrate, iminodiacetic acid and isonicotinic acid were mixed in distilled water and ethanol and stirred for 12 h at room temperature. The solution was adjusted to pH 5.0 with aqueous NaOH, sealed in a 25 mL Teflon-lined stainless-steel autoclave and heated at 180 °C under autogenous pressure for 8 days. After cooling, blue square-slice crystals were filtered, washed with ethanol and dried at room temperature for 24 h.
synthesis.temperature: Room temperature during stirring; 180 °C during solvothermal heating; room temperature during drying
synthesis.time: 12 h stirring; 8 days heating; 24 h drying
synthesis.vessel_or_method: 25 mL Teflon-lined stainless-steel autoclave; solvothermal, under autogenous pressure
synthesis.workup_and_crystallization: Cool to room temperature; filter blue square-slice crystals, wash with ethanol and dry at room temperature.

properties.summary: Weak antiferromagnetic interactions were indicated by the temperature dependence of susceptibility. The Gd analogue showed a comparatively large magnetocaloric effect.

measurements.name: χMT
measurements.conditions: Room temperature; dc susceptibility measured under 2.0 kOe

source_locations.location: Notes and references, crystal data for 1

list_of_rare_earth_compounds.structure_description: The lantern-shaped cluster has a Ni8 inner shell, Gd20 and Gd32 middle shells, and an outer Ni-containing shell. The article describes a Gd52Ni51 lantern core together with an additional Ni coordination unit, giving 52 Ni ions overall.

synthesis.procedure: Prepared by the procedure reported for 1, substituting Dy2O3 for Gd2O3: the oxide, nickel acetate tetrahydrate, iminodiacetic acid and isonicotinic acid were stirred in distilled water and ethanol for 12 h at room temperature. After adjustment to pH 5.0 with 1.0 M aqueous NaOH, the solution was sealed in a 25 mL Teflon-lined stainless-steel autoclave and heated at 180 °C under autogenous pressure for 8 days. The resulting blue square-slice crystals were isolated using the work-up reported for 1.
synthesis.temperature: Room temperature during stirring; 180 °C during solvothermal heating; room temperature during drying
synthesis.time: 12 h stirring; 8 days heating; 24 h drying
synthesis.vessel_or_method: 25 mL Teflon-lined stainless-steel autoclave; solvothermal, under autogenous pressure
synthesis.workup_and_crystallization: Cool to room temperature; filter blue square-slice crystals, wash with ethanol and dry at room temperature.

properties.summary: The article reports slow relaxation of magnetization for the Dy analogue. Its susceptibility decreases on cooling, and its measured magnetocaloric effect is smaller than that of 1.

measurements.name: χMT
measurements.conditions: 300 K; dc susceptibility measured under 2.0 kOe

source_locations.location: Notes and references, crystal data for 2

list_of_rare_earth_compounds.structure_description: The Dy52Ni51 lantern core is described as similar to that of 1, although its bridging atoms and ligands differ. A further Ni unit coordinated by acetate, glycine and water is associated with the core through hydrogen bonding, giving 52 Ni ions overall.
